results.name: multi_within_set_target_variance
results.description: Mean, over multi-example sets probed with at least 4 targets, of the variance of per-target yes rates within the set; observed > null means people discriminate between targets of the same set more sharply than the model (observed < null: model over-discriminates).
results.code:
# name: multi_within_set_target_variance
# description: Mean, over multi-example sets probed with at least 4 targets, of the variance of per-target yes rates within the set; observed > null means people discriminate between targets of the same set more sharply than the model (observed < null: model over-discriminates).
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",").values + 1
    d = df.loc[n >= 2, ["number_set", "target", "rating"]]
    pm_ = d.groupby(["number_set", "target"])["rating"].mean().reset_index()
    g = pm_.groupby("number_set")["rating"]
    v = g.var(ddof=0)
    c = g.size()
    v = v[c >= 4]
    return float(v.mean()) if len(v) else 0.0

results.name: multi_zero_consensus_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) pairs from multi-example sets where none of the 9 answers is yes; observed > null means people give unanimous "no" more often than the model, whose doubt-mode flat yes puts a floor under every target (observed < null: floor too low).
results.code:
# name: multi_zero_consensus_fraction
# description: Fraction of (set, target) pairs from multi-example sets where none of the 9 answers is yes; observed > null means people give unanimous "no" more often than the model, whose doubt-mode flat yes puts a floor under every target (observed < null: floor too low).
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",").values + 1
    d = df.loc[n >= 2, ["number_set", "target", "rating"]]
    s = d.groupby(["number_set", "target"])["rating"].sum()
    return float((s == 0).mean()) if len(s) else 0.0

results.name: odd_even_set_parity_break_asymmetry
results.description: Among multi-example sets of uniform parity, yes rate for even targets after all-odd sets minus yes rate for odd targets after all-even sets; nonzero observed vs null means parity violations are tolerated asymmetrically (odd vs even sets) in a way the model's symmetric parity treatment misses.

results.name: prime_set_prime_target_gap
results.description: On multi-example sets whose examples are all prime (e.g. 3,7 / 67,31,17,61), yes rate for prime targets minus yes rate for non-prime targets; observed > null means people infer the prime rule more sharply than the model (observed < null: model over-weights primality).
results.code:
# name: prime_set_prime_target_gap
# description: On multi-example sets whose examples are all prime (e.g. 3,7 / 67,31,17,61), yes rate for prime targets minus yes rate for non-prime targets; observed > null means people infer the prime rule more sharply than the model (observed < null: model over-weights primality).
def test_statistic(df):
    P = {n for n in range(2, 101) if all(n % k for k in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1))}
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    ok = np.zeros(len(u), bool)
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        ok[i] = len(ex) >= 2 and all(e in P for e in ex)
    m = ok[inv]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    hit = np.isin(t, list(P))
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    a, b = m & hit, m & ~hit
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: in_span_parity_break_yes
results.description: On multi-example sets of uniform parity, yes rate for opposite-parity targets that lie strictly between the smallest and largest example; observed > null means interval similarity overrides parity for people more than the model allows (observed < null: model's span term leaks yes onto parity violators).
results.code:
# name: in_span_parity_break_yes
# description: On multi-example sets of uniform parity, yes rate for opposite-parity targets that lie strictly between the smallest and largest example; observed > null means interval similarity overrides parity for people more than the model allows (observed < null: model's span term leaks yes onto parity violators).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    par = np.full(len(u), -1); lo = np.zeros(len(u)); hi = np.zeros(len(u))
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        ps = {e % 2 for e in ex}
        lo[i], hi[i] = min(ex), max(ex)
        if len(ex) >= 2 and len(ps) == 1:
            par[i] = ps.pop()
    p = par[inv]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    m = (p >= 0) & (t % 2 != p) & (t > lo[inv]) & (t < hi[inv])
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0

results.name: power_of_two_member_gap
results.description: On multi-example sets made only of powers of two (e.g. 8,16 / 16,32,2,8), yes rate for power-of-two targets minus yes rate for other targets; observed > null means people pick out the powers-of-two rule more sharply than the model (which spreads yes over even/multiple targets).

def test_statistic(df):
    pw = {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    ok = np.zeros(len(u), bool)
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        ok[i] = len(ex) >= 2 and all(e in pw for e in ex)
    m = ok[inv]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    hit = np.isin(t, list(pw))
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    a, b = m & hit, m & ~hit
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: tens_digit_lure_yes
results.description: Yes rate on multi-example sets whose examples all share a final digit d, for targets whose tens digit is d but whose final digit is not (e.g. 84,94,34 -> 40-49); observed < null means the model over-generalizes a shared final digit to "contains the digit" / tens-position lures.
results.code:
# name: tens_digit_lure_yes
# description: Yes rate on multi-example sets whose examples all share a final digit d, for targets whose tens digit is d but whose final digit is not (e.g. 84,94,34 -> 40-49); observed < null means the model over-generalizes a shared final digit to "contains the digit" / tens-position lures.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    dig = np.full(len(u), -1)
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        fd = {e % 10 for e in ex}
        if len(ex) >= 2 and len(fd) == 1:
            dig[i] = fd.pop()
    d = dig[inv]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    m = (d >= 0) & (t >= 10) & (t <= 99) & ((t // 10) == d) & ((t % 10) != d)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: mixed_parity_unpatterned_yes
results.description: Yes rate on multi-example sets with mixed parity and no shared final digit (unpatterned sets like 92,82,27,42 or 48,99,3), over all their targets; observed < null means the model's flat doubt-mode yes is too generous for sets with no shared rule (observed > null: too stingy).
results.code:
# name: mixed_parity_unpatterned_yes
# description: Yes rate on multi-example sets with mixed parity and no shared final digit (unpatterned sets like 92,82,27,42 or 48,99,3), over all their targets; observed < null means the model's flat doubt-mode yes is too generous for sets with no shared rule (observed > null: too stingy).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    u, inv = np.unique(sets, return_inverse=True)
    ok = np.zeros(len(u), bool)
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        ok[i] = len(ex) >= 2 and len({e % 2 for e in ex}) == 2 and len({e % 10 for e in ex}) > 1
    m = ok[inv]
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0
